title: store.activate ignores the owner's recorded phase (rollback to shadow does not stop activation)
reproduction: PYTHONPATH=src python auth1.py: record phase path to limited_production, approve activation grant, owner records transition to shadow (core.phase.effective -> 'shadow'), run store.activate on a Worker built with Phase.LIMITED_PRODUCTION and BRAMBLELOOP_PUBLISH_AUTHORISED=1.
observed: effective phase now: shadow / activate outputs: {'activated': True, 'state_on_etsy': 'active'} / etsy state: active
impact: The only effect that makes a listing public and charges a fee honours only the worker's boot-time phase and the env flag. An owner phase rollback (the documented kill path, F-299) is not honoured by activation (publish does re-resolve core.phase.effective, activate does not).
fix: In handle_store_activate, resolve core.phase.effective(ctx.db) at both effect-boundary checks (and before client.activate) and refuse unless in PHASES_THAT_MAY_PUBLISH; better, make Worker/ctx.phase a live property.

title: Unbilled spend: malformed model output is billed by the provider but recorded as 0 tokens / no cost row
reproduction: spend2.py: ModelGateway with registry and a provider returning ModelResponse(input_tokens=3000, output_tokens=1500) with non-JSON text; complete_json('concept.naming@1').
observed: raised MalformedModelOutput; calls=[(0,0,0.0,False),(0,0,0.0,False)]; CostEntry rows: 0; spent_this_month: 0.0 (two attempts per provider, response tokens discarded)
impact: Every malformed-JSON retry is real provider spend never counted against the CA$100 month or agent daily ceiling. Retry loops make it systematic.
fix: Record response.input_tokens/output_tokens (modelled cost, price_basis assumed) for the malformed attempt; release reservation with actual cost.

title: Image render spend is never written to the cost ledger by images.generate or most callers
reproduction: spend1.py S1: patch images._post to return an image; 3x images.generate(db=db,...).
observed: CostEntry rows: 0; spent_this_month: 0.0; reservations released with actual_cad 0.0274 each. Only image_bench and images.probe write CostEntry.
impact: The reservation is released with actual_cad but the monthly ceiling counts only CostEntry(kind=llm); render spend vanishes after release, so the CA$100 combined 'model, vision and image' ceiling and break-even/unit-cost never see it. spend_report drift even labels image rows 'reconciles by construction' while none exist.
fix: Write spend_report.record(...) inside images._generate_reserved (single writer) with price_basis assumed; make release_render do it.

title: Image provider billed-but-failed renders release the reservation as unbilled
reproduction: spend1.py S2: provider POST succeeds, returned image link cannot be fetched.
observed: ImagesRefused raised; reservation (0.0274, actual None, released); 0 cost rows
impact: After _post succeeds the provider has charged; link-fetch failure, BFL poll timeout/moderation, empty image all count as zero spend.
fix: Treat any failure after the provider POST returned 2xx as billed (record modelled cost, release with actual).

title: Ceiling check and reservation are not atomic (check-then-insert race across holders)
reproduction: spend1.py S4: two threads (distinct holders) call check_budget_cad(estimate=60) with ceiling 100; outstanding() read synchronised by a barrier to widen the natural window.
impact: Overshoot bounded by concurrent callers x estimate; real window is the gap between outstanding() and reserve() (no lock/txn; listing_costs.locked exists but is not used here). Barrier is artificial; race is real on Postgres with several workers.
fix: Do the sum + insert in one transaction under pg_advisory_xact_lock / BEGIN IMMEDIATE (as listing_costs.locked does), re-check after insert.

title: Own-holder reservations excluded from the ceiling; protection depends on callers passing uncommitted_cad
reproduction: spend1.py S3: 10 sequential check_budget_cad(estimate=40) from one holder with no release.
observed: granted 10 x CA$40 against ceiling 100.0 (no refusal)
impact: A batch loop that reserves and releases late (or forgets uncommitted_cad) can reserve 4x the month. Not shown to occur in current callers (suspected hazard).
fix: Count own live reservations too, and have callers release before re-reserving; or count own-holder reservations minus declared uncommitted.

title: Readiness 'sustainable_economics' passes on assumed sales volume and partial cost data
reproduction: sust1.py: one DRAFT listing at CA$8, 25 llm CostEntry rows (CA$0.50 total, 5 tagged to the product), zero orders.
observed: sustainable: True | steady-state economics are sustainable at opening prices; base: contribution_monthly 417.6 (60 assumed sales/month x modelled per-sale), ai cost 0.9. break_even row 'reading: computed', break_even_sales 1.
impact: Sustainability gate input is entirely assumed sales (SCENARIOS) x modelled fees; image spend (B2), untagged/ads/hosting are excluded; output never states volume is assumed, and the readiness requirement is ready=True. Missing data (no sales, no creation cost beyond tagged rows) yields a green gate, contradicting 'UNKNOWN is never zero'.
fix: Require measured orders (or label verdict 'ASSUMED' and keep ready=False until sales observed); include all spend kinds and untracked-render gaps; mark break_even 'floor' when creation cost is partial.

title: Phase transition seal is replayable: copying an old sealed 'production' row as newest restores production
reproduction: auth2.py: record shadow->...->production, then rollback to shadow, then (DB writer, no token) insert a copy of the old sealed 'limited_production->production' AuditLog row.
observed: after rollback: shadow; after replay of old sealed row: production True 'recorded limited_production -> production' (env agrees, no incident)
impact: Seal binds content only; no nonce/sequence/prev-hash/expiry. latest_recorded() trusts the newest verifying row, so a replay defeats an owner rollback and the 'forged row' defence the module claims.
fix: Chain transitions: seal includes prev transition id/hash and the record must have from == the verified previous 'to'; reject duplicates of an existing seal.

title: Grant revocation is unsealed: deleting the revocation row revives a revoked publication/activation grant
reproduction: auth2.py: sealed grant, pa.revoke(), delete the owner.publication.revoked AuditLog row, call _check_one.
observed: after deleting revocation row: refusal= None (grant valid again, within 24h)
impact: Revocation is plain append-only audit row with no seal; also anyone able to insert audit rows can DoS any grant. Needs DB write access (not the token).
fix: Seal revocations under the ops token and bind to grant seal; treat unsealed revocation as revoking (fail closed) but a missing one detectable via audit chain.

title: Authority enforced only at the pipeline call site, not inside EtsyClient (create_draft/activate need only env flag + phase / any non-empty string)
reproduction: read only: EtsyClient(phase=limited_production, owner_authorised=True).activate('1', launch_authorisation='x') passes _require; activate() only checks non-empty string.
impact: Any new caller of the client bypasses the sealed grant; defence in depth gap.
fix: Make client require a verified grant object (id + validate callback) for create_draft/activate.

title: Upward phase transition accepts arbitrary evidence refs; no check that readiness/rollback evidence exists or passes
reproduction: read: refs only need non-empty strings for keys readiness and rollback.
impact: Owner-token holder can step to production on fabricated refs; the audit trail looks complete.
fix: Resolve refs against launch.readiness / rollback records.

title: Receipt status 'partially refunded' with no refunds[] rows is booked as an unrefunded paid sale
reproduction: orders1.py A: receipt status='partially refunded', refunds=[].
observed: order revenue 10.0, refunded False, contribution 8.77, state paid
impact: Revenue/contribution overstated until a ledger refund entry (unit UNVERIFIED) shows; the status Etsy gave is dropped.
fix: Treat partially refunded without a refund amount as UNKNOWN/held for refund amount; flag order and exclude from 'measured'.

title: Fully refunded/cancelled first order is kept as 'the first sale' and counted as order and customer
reproduction: orders2.py/orders4.py: paid receipt, then same receipt canceled with higher update_timestamp.
observed: first_sale record payload price_cad 10.0 for etsy:2:20 with no state; P&L: gross 10, refunds 10, net 0, orders 1, customers 1, trajectory observed_orders 1
impact: 'First truthful sale' milestone and cost-per-acquired-customer / AOV count a voided sale; first_sale payload never refreshes its state.
fix: Exclude fully_refunded/cancelled from order & customer counts (report separately) and pick first sale from net-positive paid orders; refresh payload on state change.

title: A paid sale in a currency with no stored rate (EUR/GBP/AUD) is written nowhere while books read 'measured'
observed: orders [] ; not_recorded [{'why': 'no rate on file for EUR...'}]; ran True; only the audit row detail carries it, no incident/owner action
impact: Real revenue and the real first customer vanish from ledger/customers/first_sale; cursor advances; P&L reports sales_reading measured with undercount.
fix: Record the order with unconverted amount and basis UNKNOWN FX (or open an incident/owner action and mark sales INCOMPLETE).

title: Partial ledger fee reads as 'measured' and is not reflected in order detail/basis text
reproduction: orders3.py K: only a 'transaction' ledger entry (0.65) posted for a CA$10 sale.
observed: fees_basis 'measured', fees_cad 0.65 (model 1.23), contribution 9.35, reconciliation partial_etsy_ledger, but detail.money.contribution_basis still 'ESTIMATED fees'; books all_observed counts fees as measured
impact: Contribution overstated and labelled measured before processing fee posts; books all_figures_observed can be true on partial fees.
fix: Keep 'modelled'/'partial' basis (take max(model, measured) for missing kinds) until EXPECTED_PER_ORDER kinds present; treat partial as not observed in books.all_observed.

title: Ledger refund/fee classification by substring: a fee credit named *_refund is booked as a customer refund; ledger units UNVERIFIED with no plausibility bound
reproduction: orders3.py M (ledger_type 'transaction_fee_refund', amount +65c) and L (amount 6500 on a CA$10 sale).
observed: M: revenue 10.00 -> 9.35, ledger_refund_cad 0.65, fees unchanged 1.23. L: fees measured 65.0, contribution -55.0 (no sanity cap)
impact: Real ledger_type strings and LEDGER_AMOUNT_DIVISOR=100 were never read from a live shop (module says so) yet results are stamped measured. A unit error silently produces measured losses.
fix: Classify fee reversals before refunds; quarantine entries whose fee exceeds e.g. 50% of price as unclassified; do not flip to measured until a live read validates units.

title: Refund currency ignored; duplicate transaction_ids in a receipt collapse to one line
reproduction: orders1.py D, I: USD 5.00 refund on CAD receipt; duplicated transaction id.
observed: D: revenue 5.0 (USD refund read as CAD); I: one order of 10.0, duplicate silently dropped
fix: Compare refund currency to line currency (convert/refuse); refuse receipts with duplicate transaction ids.

title: Product spend attribution trusted from job inputs (cir.slug) and caller-supplied 'shared' detail
reproduction: read only: job_product returns cir.slug without catalogue check; detail={'attribution':'shared'} keeps spend untagged.
impact: Per-product creation cost (break-even) can be misattributed or hidden; total ceiling unaffected.
fix: Verify slug against Product/Listing even when cir present; log when shared overrides inside a product job.

title: Publication evidence labels listing price 'measured' and sales_volume 'measured' if any order (incl. cancelled) exists
fix: Label price 'set by owner'; count net-positive orders only.
